slack.messaging.description: Send, read, react to messages in Slack conversations

slack.typing.description: Show typing as a status on a pending addressed thread

slack.history.description: Fetch message and thread history from Slack conversations

slack.subscriptions.description: Manage per-conversation ambient-message subscriptions (which conversations deliver non-mention messages for passive awareness). Mentions and DMs are always delivered and are not affected by subscriptions.

toolText.name: send_message
toolText.description: Send a message to a Slack conversation (channel, private channel, DM, or group DM). Supports Slack mrkdwn; use <@USER_ID> for mentions (find_user resolves names to IDs).

channelId.description: Slack conversation ID (C… channel, G… private/group, D… DM)

toolText.name: reply_message
toolText.description: Reply in a thread of a Slack conversation. Incoming messages show `thread=` when they are already in a thread and `id=` always. Pass the `thread=` value if the message you answer shows one; otherwise pass its `id=`, which starts a thread under it. In fetch_history and fetch_thread results, pass its `rootTs`, which names the thread it's in, or the message itself.

messageId.description: Thread ID (ts): the message's `thread=` if it has one, else its `id=`; in fetch_history and fetch_thread results, its `rootTs`

toolText.name: upload_file
toolText.description: Upload a file to a Slack conversation, optionally into a thread and with a message. Pass the file as text (content) or as base64 (contentBase64), not both: at most 5 MiB of file bytes, after base64 is decoded or text is encoded as UTF-8. Same write rules as send_message.

filename.description: File name shown in Slack, with extension (e.g. positions.csv)

contentBase64.description: File contents as canonical RFC 4648 base64 with required padding, for binary files; no whitespace or data URI prefix

messageId.description: Thread to upload into: the message's `thread=` if it has one, else its `id=`; in fetch_history and fetch_thread results, its `rootTs`

comment.description: Message posted with the file (Slack mrkdwn)

title.description: Title shown above the file; defaults to the file name

toolText.name: send_dm
toolText.description: Send a direct message to a Slack user (opens the DM conversation if needed)

toolText.name: add_reaction
toolText.description: Add an emoji reaction to a Slack message

emoji.description: Emoji name, with or without colons (e.g. thumbsup or :thumbsup:)

toolText.name: edit_message
toolText.description: Edit a message sent by this bot

toolText.name: delete_message
toolText.description: Delete a message sent by this bot

toolText.name: list_channels
toolText.description: List Slack conversations: channels the bot is a member of, private channels, and, unless this host has turned direct messages off, DMs and group DMs: each kind the bot's token has the read scope for. An answer that leaves out a kind the token can't read says which, beside the list. Set includeNonMember to also list public channels the bot has not joined (it cannot receive events from or post to those without being invited).

includeNonMember.description: Also include public channels the bot is not a member of (default false)

toolText.name: refresh_channels
toolText.description: Re-scan the Slack conversations the bot is in and register any that the host does not yet know about. Use this if the bot was invited to a new channel after startup and it is not showing up in your channel list.

toolText.name: fetch_history
toolText.description: Fetch message history from a Slack conversation, oldest-first. Covers channel-level messages only — replies inside threads are not returned (use fetch_thread for those), so an active thread can look quiet here. Use `oldest`/`latest` (message IDs / ts values) to bound the range. Substring and exact author-ID predicates are ANDed. Check pagination.scanComplete and stopReason: zero bounded matches does not prove absence. To go on to older messages, call again with the same arguments and cursor set to pagination.nextCursor.

maxScanned.description: Candidate messages scanned per call, independently of returned matches

maxBytes.description: Maximum UTF-8 bytes of the complete result JSON. A message that does not fit beside the ones before it is left for the next call

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from an earlier call, with the same channel, thread, time bounds and filters

limit.description: Maximum matching messages returned per call

textContains.description: Literal substring of a message's content as returned, except that a mentioned user appears only by their user ID, as @U… (uid:U…), not by name; case-insensitive by default; no regex

caseSensitive.description: Use exact case for textContains; otherwise JavaScript Unicode toLowerCase, without normalization

authorIds.description: Match any exact author ID, a message's authorId or authorBotId, AND textContains; missing authors do not match

toolText.name: fetch_thread
toolText.description: Fetch a bounded part of one Slack thread, oldest-first (parent first on a call without oldest or cursor). Pass the thread's parent id: a reply's thread=, a message's own id= when it shows no thread=, or a message's rootTs in fetch_history or fetch_thread results. Check pagination.scanComplete and stopReason. To go on to newer replies, call again with the same arguments and cursor set to pagination.nextCursor.

maxScanned.description: Candidate messages scanned per call, independently of returned matches

maxBytes.description: Maximum UTF-8 bytes of the complete result JSON. A message that does not fit beside the ones before it is left for the next call

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from an earlier call, with the same channel, thread, time bounds and filters

threadTs.description: Parent message ID (ts) of the thread

limit.description: Maximum messages returned, including the parent when present

toolText.name: find_user
toolText.description: Find Slack users by name (username, real name, or display name substring). Returns user IDs for mentions and DMs — use <@USER_ID> in message text to mention.

toolText.name: fetch_attachment
toolText.description: Fetch a Slack file attachment by URL and return its bytes inline: images as image blocks, text-ish files decoded, other binary as base64. URLs come from incoming message attachment refs (url_private, fetched with bot auth). Max 5MB.

url.description: Full url_private of the Slack file (https://files.slack.com/…)

toolText.name: subscribe_channel
toolText.description: Subscribe to ambient (non-mention) messages from a Slack conversation. Direct mentions and DMs always come through regardless of subscriptions; this only controls passive awareness of channel chatter. Persisted across restarts.

channelId.description: Slack conversation ID to subscribe to

toolText.name: unsubscribe_channel
toolText.description: Stop receiving ambient messages from a Slack conversation. Mentions and DMs from there will still arrive. Persisted across restarts.

channelId.description: Slack conversation ID to unsubscribe from

toolText.name: list_subscriptions
toolText.description: List the Slack conversations subscribed for ambient message delivery. When every member conversation is subscribed (member mode), lists the muted ones instead.
